label: Linear Systems and Time Series
notes: Spanning printed pages 215 through 227, this chapter recasts a stationary signal as a single point on a statistical manifold rather than as a recorded waveform. We treat the spectral density as the geometric object and read AR and MA models as finite-dimensional submanifolds carrying dual flat structure.

label: A Process as a Point
notes: The central move is representation. A long observed waveform collapses to one coordinate vector once we accept stationarity and Gaussianity, so the whole signal becomes a point. The manifold's tangent directions are parameter perturbations, and nearby points are processes whose second-order statistics differ only slightly.

label: Spectral Density Representation
notes: By Bochner's theorem the autocovariance sequence and the spectral density are Fourier duals, both encoding the same Gaussian law. The spectrum must stay strictly positive, which is the manifold's interior constraint. We coordinate a process by its spectrum and verify positivity numerically before trusting any picture drawn over it.

label: AR and MA Submanifolds
notes: Autoregressive and moving-average models are finite-dimensional submanifolds of the full process space. AR places poles inside the unit circle and MA places zeros, so their spectra are reciprocal in form. Stability requires roots inside the disc, which bounds each coordinate region with a curved stationarity frontier.

label: Spectral Perturbation
notes: Perturbing one parameter deforms the spectral curve, and the size of that deformation defines distance on the manifold. A change near a pole stretches the spectrum sharply, signalling an ill-conditioned, steep metric direction. Watching the curve move makes the Fisher geometry visible instead of merely asserted.

label: The Whittle Fisher Metric
notes: The Whittle approximation turns the Gaussian likelihood into a frequency-domain integral, giving a clean closed form for the Fisher metric. Two parameter perturbations are compared by integrating their log-spectrum derivatives against frequency. This integral is the inner product that decides which moves on the manifold are short or expensive.

label: Dual Coordinates
notes: AR filter coefficients and the autocovariance sequence are dual charts on the same family. One view is straight under the exponential connection, the other under the mixture connection. Filter-like and moment-like scales diverge near the stationarity boundary, the operational signature of the dually flat structure carried by these models.

label: e-flat versus m-flat
notes: AR models are e-flat: linear in the natural log-spectrum coordinates supplied by filter parameters. MA models are m-flat in the dual sense. The exponential and mixture connections are orthogonal under the Fisher metric, so the two families realise the dual flat skeleton of the whole process manifold.

label: Prediction Error as Divergence
notes: One-step prediction error behaves like a divergence surface over parameter space, minimised at the true process and curving upward around it. Its Hessian at the minimum reproduces the Whittle Fisher metric, tying optimal prediction directly to the manifold's geometry and to the Kolmogorov-Szego formula for the error floor.

label: Recap and Habits
notes: Closing pages 215 to 227, keep three habits. Name the geometric object, here the positive spectrum, before reading an algorithm. Ask which metric, the Whittle Fisher form, shapes each update. Always pair a visual claim with a numerical invariant such as spectral positivity or an autocovariance positive-semidefinite check.
